why_incorrect.C: The Citations feature cannot be combined with `output_config.format`; the request returns a 400, so this design does not work as described.
why_incorrect.D: A bibliography shows which files were used but not which statement came from where.

questions.scenario: Kestrel Robotics builds supplier risk profiles by extracting facts from filings and press releases. For one supplier, an annual report gives a headcount of 4,200 and an investor presentation gives 3,650. The current pipeline keeps whichever value it extracted last.
questions.question: Which two changes best handle this? (Select 2)

options.A: Require each extracted figure to carry its publication or data-collection date along with the source document
options.B: Keep both values in the profile, each annotated with its source, and flag the conflict for the reconciliation step
options.C: Keep the more recent document's value and discard the other, since newer documents supersede older ones
options.D: Store the average of the two values as the supplier's headcount, since the true figure is probably between them
options.E: Keep the value from the source with the higher authority and drop the other one so that the profile stays clean

questions.explanation: Conflicting figures from credible sources should be preserved with attribution and flagged so a later step or person decides how to reconcile them. Recording dates matters because many apparent contradictions are just figures from different periods.

why_incorrect.C: Newer documents can report older periods; without collection dates, recency of publication is an unreliable tiebreaker.
why_incorrect.D: An average is a number no source reported and loses both originals.
why_incorrect.E: Dropping a credible value hides the conflict and the evidence a reviewer needs to judge it.

questions.scenario: Halvard Policy Institute's research system finds two credible surveys on remote work in public agencies: one reports 31% of staff working remotely, the other 44%. The synthesis agent has been choosing one figure, or labelling the pair a contradiction. The surveys were collected in 2023 and 2025.
questions.question: How should the system handle the two figures?

options.A: Report only the more recent figure, since newer data always supersedes older data in any research report
options.B: Report the figure from the source with higher domain authority, and drop the other one to avoid confusing readers
options.C: Keep both figures with sources and dates, present the gap as a likely change over time, and note method differences
options.D: Average the two figures and cite both sources, so the report gives its readers one single number they can use directly

questions.explanation: Subagents should carry publication or collection dates so temporal differences are not misread as contradictions. Here the 2023 and 2025 dates likely explain the gap, so the report should present both figures with attribution as a probable change over time. Dates often explain apparent contradictions, but comparability still has to be checked: differences in sampling, definitions of 'remote' or agency mix should be noted rather than hidden.

why_incorrect.A: Dropping the earlier figure loses the trend and hides that a second credible source exists.
why_incorrect.B: Picking one credible source arbitrarily discards evidence and may hide a real change over time.
why_incorrect.D: Averaging measurements from different years produces a number that neither survey supports.

questions.scenario: Ashgrove Research's subagents return polished prose summaries. By the time the synthesis and report steps finish, many statements in the final report carry no citation, and some citations point to the wrong source.
questions.question: Which TWO changes best preserve provenance through the pipeline? (Choose 2.)

options.A: Have the synthesis agent cite the subagent that supplied each claim, since that subagent's logs show where it came from
options.B: Keep prose summaries but list every source consulted in a bibliography at the end of the final report
options.C: Require synthesis to keep those claim-source links when merging, combining sources when several subagents report the same claim
options.D: Have subagents return each claim with its source URL, a supporting excerpt and the publication date, as structured records
options.E: Have the report agent add citations at the end by searching the web for pages that appear to support each sentence of the draft

questions.explanation: Attribution is lost when findings are compressed into prose without claim-to-source mappings. Structured claim records (claim, URL or document, excerpt, date) from subagents, preserved and merged through synthesis, keep every statement traceable to the evidence behind it.

why_incorrect.A: An internal agent name is not a source; readers need the original document, and logs are not part of the report.
why_incorrect.B: A bibliography does not show which source supports which claim, so readers cannot check individual statements.
why_incorrect.E: Retrofitting citations may attach sources that were never consulted and do not support the claim as stated.
